query: How should sensor noise, communication delays, and model uncertainty be modeled and incorporated into training and a robust or stochastic MPC formulation?

response.query: How should sensor noise, communication delays, and model uncertainty be modeled and incorporated into training and a robust or stochastic MPC formulation?
response.answer: Sensor noise, communication delays, and model uncertainty in robust or stochastic Model Predictive Control (MPC) are modeled using probabilistic frameworks, incorporating uncertainty distributions and delay bounds, and optimizing cost functions that account for these uncertainties during training.

results.content: Interactive Imitation Learning in Robotics: A Survey Carlos Celemin∗ Delft University of Technology c.e.celeminpaez@tudelft.nl Rodrigo Pérez-Dattari∗ Delft University of Technology r.j.perezdattari@tudelft.nl Eugenio Chisari∗ University of Freiburg chisari@cs.uni-freiburg.de Giovanni Franzese∗ Delft University of Technology g.franzese@tudelft.nl Leandro de Souza Rosa Delft University of Technology l.desouzarosa@tudelft.nl Ravi Prakash Delft University of Technology r.prakash-1@tudelft.nl Zlatan Ajanović Delft University of Technology z.ajanovic@tudelft.nl Marta Ferraz Delft University of Technology m.ferraz@tudelft.nl Abhinav Valada University of Freiburg valada@cs.uni-freiburg.de Jens Kober Delft University of Technology j.kober@tudelft.nl November 2, 2022 Abstract Interactive Imitation Learning (IIL) is a branch of Imitation Learning (IL) where human feedback is provided intermittently during robot execution allowing an online improvement of the robot’s behavior. Some recent methods enable human teachers to train robots through evaluative feedback, like Learning from Critique (LfC), or Interactive Reinforcement Learning (Interactive RL), in which the teachers provide feedback that rates the desirability of the exhibited behavior during training time.
